Chess Elo Prediction — 1D CNN over Move Sequences¶

Architecture: Multi-scale 1D CNN replacing the BiLSTM in v4. Three parallel convolutional branches with kernel sizes 3, 5, and 7 capture short, medium, and longer-range move patterns simultaneously. Global max-pooling produces a fixed-size vector regardless of game length.

Why it might work better: CNNs parallelise fully over the sequence dimension — no sequential dependency at all — making them considerably faster than LSTMs on CPU. Multiple kernel sizes are useful here because chess patterns operate at different scales: a local tactic might span 3 moves, while a strategic plan could take 7 moves to execute. Capturing both simultaneously and letting the model decide which is relevant is a known strength of multi-scale convolution (it's how TextCNN works for text classification).

Honest tradeoff: CNNs have bounded receptive fields (max 7 moves here). Very long-range dependencies — a positional weakness established in move 10 that only matters in move 50 — are invisible to the CNN unless the filters happen to catch them by coincidence. This is the opposite failure mode from LSTMs, which can in principle see long-range context but tend to forget it in practice. Whether chess games actually have important long-range dependencies that LSTMs exploit is unclear, which is exactly why this experiment is worth running.

What HPO searches over: number of filters per branch, dropout.

Baseline to beat: v4 combined MAE ≈ 200 Elo.

Model — Multi-Scale 1D CNN¶

Sequence branch: token embedding (with clock + turn appended) → three parallel Conv1d branches with kernel sizes 3, 5, 7 → global max-pool each → concatenate (3 × N_FILTERS features).

Static branch: same MLP as v4.

Fusion: concat CNN output + static → shared trunk → two output heads.

Padding ensures all convolutions produce the same sequence length before max-pool.

Model built — 947,568 trainable parameters  |  N_FILTERS=128  seq_dim=384

Hyperparameter Optimisation (Optuna)¶

15 trials on a 50k-game subset, 3 training epochs each. Searches:

  • n_filters: filters per CNN branch {64, 128, 256}
  • embed_dim: move embedding dimension {32, 64, 128}
  • dropout: regularisation strength {0.1 … 0.4}

Kernel sizes (3, 5, 7) are fixed as the architectural choice — they define the model identity.

Best trial: 11. Best value: 0.75491: 100%|██████████| 15/15 [59:35<00:00, 238.38s/it] 
Best trial  val_loss=0.7549
Best params: {'n_filters': 64, 'embed_dim': 128, 'dropout': 0.11161755998835499}

Full training will use: n_filters=64  embed_dim=128  dropout=0.112
